Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicantSanjay Shukla Alias Kaushal Kumar Shukla, with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No.820 of 2017, under Sections-366, 376,
406 I.P.C. Police Station Gilaula, District Shrawasti.
It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that the prosecutrix under Section 161 Cr.P.C.has made allegation of rape against co-accused Mintoo.

sentences.text: Thereafter, under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she made allegation of rape against applicant, his father Lallu and Peshkar.

Learned counsel submitted that the court below has granted bail to co-accused Mintoo on the ground that co-accused Mintoo is married to prosecutrix and the court come to the conclusion that allegation of rape is false against him i.e. why bail was granted.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that Lallu, father of applicant was also involved in abduction of girl.
However, allegation of rape has been made against Mintoo (her husband).
As per medical report, the age of the girl is 17-18 and there is no external or internal injury found on the person of the prosecutrix.
The applicant has no criminal history.
The applicant is in jail since 26.04.2022.
Learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the applicant has committed heinous offence therefore, his bail is liable to be rejected.

Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and after hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering that co-accused Mintoo has been granted bail as well as statement of the prosecutrix recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. and medical report, I find it to be a fit case for bail.

Let the applicant,Sanjay Shukla Alias Kaushal Kumar Shukla, be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

entities.text: Sanjay Shukla Alias Kaushal Kumar Shukla
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
